```{r graph 1 -spaghetti pct change}
# rates over time, need to set a factor order for the rate_yr, OR map them to years. 
#will now try group by property number then calculate the year on year percentage change, 

graph_1_data <- wdc_rates %>%
  arrange(property_no, rate_yr) %>%
  group_by(property_no) %>%
  mutate(pct_change = (`total rates` - lag(`total rates`)) / lag(`total rates`) * 100,
         pct_change = replace_na(pct_change, 0)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(property_no, rate_yr, `total rates`, pct_change) %>%
  filter(property_no != 6318) #remove outlier

graph_1_summary <- graph_1_data %>% 
  group_by(rate_yr) %>%
  summarise(median_pct = median(pct_change),
            mean_pct = mean(pct_change),
            .groups = 'drop')
  
#spaghetti plot
#property 6318 has a 13464.58% rates change. That is odd. I will drop it. A commerical property that was increasedd from42 to 5710 in 24_25
graph_1 <- graph_1_data %>% 
ggplot(aes(x = rate_yr, y = pct_change, group = property_no)) +
  geom_line(col = "#6190F7", alpha = 0.15, linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_line(data = graph_1_summary, aes(x = rate_yr, y = median_pct, group = 1), col = "#DC0100", linewidth = 1) +
  theme(legend.position = 'none')

# I think this is pretty good for a start, maybe trim out more outliers so audience can see the pct change around the median. 
```







```{r graph 2 - fan chart pct change}
graph_2_data <- graph_1_data %>%
  # filter(pct_change < 100) %>%
  group_by(rate_yr) %>%
  summarise(
    median = median(pct_change),
    mean = mean(pct_change),
    lower25 = quantile(pct_change, 0.375),
    upper25 = quantile(pct_change, 0.625),
    lower50 = quantile(pct_change, 0.25),
    upper50 = quantile(pct_change, 0.75),
    lower90 = quantile(pct_change, 0.05),
    upper90 = quantile(pct_change, 0.95),
    lower100 = quantile(pct_change, 0),
    upper100 = quantile(pct_change, 1),
  )

graph_2 <- ggplot(data = graph_2_data, aes(x = rate_yr, group = 1)) +
  # geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower100, ymax = upper100), fill = "#6190F7", alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower90, ymax = upper90, fill = "90%"), alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower50, ymax = upper50, fill = "50%"), alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower25, ymax = upper25, fill = "25%"), alpha = 0.9) +
  geom_line(aes(y=median, color = "Median change"), linewidth = 1) +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_fill_manual(
  name = "Qunatiles",
  values = c("90%" = "#6190F7", 
             "50%" = "#6190F7", 
             "25%" = "#6190F7")
  ) + 
  scale_color_manual(
    name = "Estimates",
    values = c("Median change" = "#DC0100")
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
      plot.title = element_text(size = 17),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 13),
      axis.title.y = element_text(size = 13),
      axis.title.x = element_text(size = 13))

graph_2
  
```

```{r graph 3 map setup}
nz <- read_sf("https://www.massey.ac.nz/~jcmarsha/data/nz_map/sa3_data.sqlite")

```


```{r graph 3 map, fig.width=10, fig.height= 10}
ta_nz <- nz %>% 
  group_by(territorial_authority, regional_council) %>%
  summarise(geometry = st_union(GEOMETRY), .groups = 'drop')

whanganui <- nz %>% filter(territorial_authority == "Whanganui District")
bbox <- st_bbox(whanganui)

# w_bbox <- list(x = c(1751098, 1815702), x=c(5565628, 5655993))

w_bbox <- list(x = c(1767500, 1779000), y=c(5574000, 5585000))

nz %>% filter(territorial_authority == "Whanganui District") %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(mapping=aes(fill = sa3_name)) +
  coord_sf(xlim = w_bbox$x, ylim = w_bbox$y) +
  geom_sf_label(mapping=aes(label=sa3_name), size=3) +
  guides(fill = 'none')
```

```{r}
#getting the streets int he suburbs. To then go map to suburbs manually. 
graph_3_data <- wdc_rates %>%
  mutate(
    suburb = recode(suburb,
    "Bastia/Durie Hills Putiki" = "Bastia-Durie Hill-Putiki",
    "Whanganui Central" = "Whanganui Centre",
    "Whanganui Rural" = "Whanganui District Rural",)
  ) %>%
  group_by(suburb) %>%
  summarise(median_rates = median(`total rates`, .groups = 'drop'))

#what to do about st john and otamtea? I may try mapping streets to the releavant suburb. Will split the string to get street then google search I guess. 
streets <- wdc_rates %>% 
  filter(suburb == "St Johns/Otamatea") %>% 
  select(property_address, suburb) %>%
  mutate(
    street = str_remove(property_address, "~.*"),
    street = str_remove(street, "-."),
    street = str_remove(street, "^(?i:unit\\s+)?(?:[\\d/][\\d/A-Za-z]*\\s+)+"), #handles numbers and numbers like 9A,alos UNIT 6C / 59 and
  ) %>%
  group_by(street) %>%
  summarise(count = n())
```
